findings: Extra first DOWN/DBLCLK already appears in separate PeekMessage PM_REMOVE results; callbacks each match a separate dispatched message.
Independent sender processes reproduce the initial single/double/drag failure, excluding self-process injection as a necessary trigger.
Initializing only the owned target thread active window with SetActiveWindow (no warmup click and unchanged foreground) restores single/double/drag sequences, including external sender processes.
SetActiveWindow(nullptr) attempt did not clear GetActiveWindow in the active-reset case; that case cannot prove behavior after clearing thread active state.
limits: A queued duplicate is observed, but root cause in OS/drivers/input routing is not established. Callback stacks do not rule out hooks elsewhere.
The target remains an owned diagnostic window, not an arbitrary external application or a formal network viewer acceptance.
No change to product input behavior, no forced foreground activation, click filtering, global hook or AttachThreadInput workaround.
Fresh SW_SHOWNOACTIVATE window with no prior thread active state remains a valid failing boundary, not removed from the acceptance requirements.
All 12 diagnostics ended without held left button or observed external input; installed services unchanged and four temporary uploads removed.
